 Search The Site New York State Puts HAULT on Minimum Wage Increase New York State Puts HAULT on Minimum Wage Increase
 Rob Banks Rob Banks Published: November 16, 2026 2299546313 Share on Facebook 
 New York State is stopping any minimum wage increase.
 Usually, New York State residents are used to an increase in minimum wage and Governor Hochul and the State has said no to any increase. Businesses around the State are happy with the stoppage because so many are siting that it has been really hard to operate a business in New York State. The biggest expense for a company typically is their labor.
 Ten years ago, in 2016, minimum wage across New York State (excluding New York City) was only $9.70. How much money were you making minimum wage for New York State.
 What is the minimum wage right now?
 $17.00 for the New York City region
 $16.00 for the rest of New York State
 There is a little bit of a loophole though to the law. There is one CERTAIN minimum wage that is going up and that is for home care pay. Home care aids, whether it be family members or company paid, the minimum wage is going up. New York State will pay you to be a home aid for a family member that is in need of verified care approved through New York State. According to the New York State website :
 the minimum wage rate for home care aides will rise on January 1, 2027 to $20.00 per hour in New York City, Long Island and Westchester County and $19.00 per hour for the rest of the state. These rates will increase by inflation but are capped at $3.00 over the standard minimum wage.
 It is important to note that there is no set increase for 2028 and that will be based off of federal and New York State inflation in the future.
